name: RECKTENWALD, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court did not err in finding zero fair market rental value for the temporarily taken land and that sovereign immunity bars attorneys' fees in inverse condemnation cases.

name: RECKTENWALD, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the ICA erred in its ruling on expert testimony foundation and that Spies's detention and initial incriminating statements were lawful, with subsequent Miranda violations being harmless error.

name: DEVENS, J.
description: Concurred, argued that a recorded judgment lien is a constitutionally protected property interest requiring personal notice for junior lienholders, but this ruling applies prospectively only due to reliance on prior law and potential prejudice to the Spences.

name: Todd W. Eddins
description: Concurred, argued that recording custodial interrogations is a necessary procedural safeguard under the Hawaiʻi Constitution's due process clause to protect rights against self-incrimination, confrontation, and a fair trial, and that modern technology makes it feasible.

name: Richard W. Pollack
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion of the court, finding that the circuit court failed to meet the procedural and substantive requirements for sealing documents and erred in denying Grube's right to self-representation.

name: Todd W. Eddins
description: Concurred, argued that the Hawaiʻi Constitution requires a strict separation of church and state, broader than the federal Establishment Clause, and that the Roberts Court's recent jurisprudence on religion is flawed and should not control state constitutional interpretation.

name: Lisa M. Ginoza
description: Concurred, argued that HRS § 657-1.8(a) is a statute of limitations and does not violate the ex post facto clause, and while the jury instructions on criminal statutes were erroneous, the error was harmless due to overwhelming evidence of the defendant's admitted conduct constituting criminal offenses at the time they occurred.

name: Sabrina S. McKenna
description: Concurred, argued that under the Hawaiʻi Constitution, the ultimate inquiry for "interrogation" is whether a law enforcement officer knew or should have known their words or conduct were reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response, even if "normally attendant to arrest and custody." The court affirmed suppression of some of Hoffman's statements but reversed for others.

name: MCKENNA, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the Commission failed to justify its instream flow standards decisions, did not adequately protect Native Hawaiian rights, lacked transparent calculations, and unlawfully delegated its public trust duties, thus requiring vacatur and remand.

name: Mark E. Recktenwald, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the state's constitutional and statutory provisions do not violate the Sixth and Fourteenth Amendments, and that the indictment was sufficient under the liberal construction standard because Tran was not prejudiced and the charge stated a crime.

name: McKENNA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Act 14 of 1995 does not preclude the plaintiffs' claims, the MKAR is not a state highway, and the State breached its constitutional and fiduciary obligation by failing to comply with the HHCA.

name: MCKENNA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Hawai'i Constitution's due process clause required a pre-deprivation contested case hearing for houseless individuals before their personal property could be seized and destroyed.

name: Todd W. Eddins
description: Concurred, argued that Hawaiʻi's Constitution does not afford an individual right to carry firearms in public for self-defense, and state firearm regulations do not violate federal constitutional rights.

name: WILSON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the anonymous jury violated defendants' constitutional rights to presumption of innocence, an impartial jury, effective assistance of counsel, and an impartial tribunal, constituting structural error that necessitates a new trial.

name: MCKENNA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Miranda warnings are required when probable cause to arrest has developed, and that Hewitt was in custody under the totality of circumstances even before probable cause developed, thus overruling *Sagapolutele-Silva*.

name: NAKAYAMA, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision to overrule *Sagapolutele-Silva* and reinstate *Ketchum*'s bright-line rule for Miranda custody was incorrect.

name: RECKTENWALD, C.J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the burden of proof remains with the challenging party, but the Ka Pa'akai framework applies to administrative rulemaking, requiring agencies to conduct a contemporaneous analysis of Native Hawaiian rights.

name: MCKENNA, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, agreeing with most of the majority opinion but disagreeing with the requirement for agencies to engage in a contemporaneous Ka Pa'akai analysis during rulemaking.

name: WILSON, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the State's unreasonable delay in sentencing deprived the defendant of due process and a fundamentally fair sentencing proceeding, and that the delay also deprived the defendant of the opportunity for allocution.

name: EDDINS, J.
description: Concurred, argued that HRS § 801-1 plainly requires a grand jury indictment for felony prosecutions and was not implicitly repealed.

name: MCKENNA, J.
description: Concurred with the majority's outcome, but also agreed with Justice Nakayama's constitutional argument that the State's prosecution was unconstitutional.

name: NAKAYAMA, J.
description: Concurred in the result of dismissing charges due to unconstitutional prosecution, but dissented from the majority's statutory interpretation, believing the 1982 amendment invalidated HRS § 801-1.

name: RECKTENWALD, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the 1982 constitutional amendment superseded HRS § 801-1, allowing felony charges via preliminary hearing.

name: RECKTENWALD, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the "totality of the circumstances" test, not probable cause alone, determines custody for Miranda purposes, and Sagapolutele-Silva was not in custody until after the SFST.

name: MCKENNA, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision overrules well-established precedent, reducing constitutional rights by eliminating the bright-line rule that probable cause triggers Miranda warnings.

name: WILSON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority "eviscerates the constitutional protection" against self-incrimination by rejecting the settled presumption that probable cause to arrest means a person is not free to leave police custody.

name: EDDINS, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Reapportionment Commission has discretion to consider, but not necessarily effectuate, the 'district within district' guidelines, and did not abuse its discretion in adopting the Plan.

name: MCKENNA, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Commission was required to effectuate the 'district within district' provision where practicable, and failed to enforce the constitution's plain language by treating mandatory criteria as discretionary.

name: WILSON, J.
description: Dissented, joined Justice McKenna's opinion arguing that the Commission was required to effectuate the 'district within district' provision where practicable.

name: NAKAYAMA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the three readings requirement mandates that a bill retain some resemblance to earlier versions, and Act 84's non-germane amendment violated this by not restarting the readings.

name: RECKTENWALD, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Constitution's plain language does not define what a "reading" entails or compel amendments to be germane, and the legislature's rules were properly followed.

name: CIRCUIT JUDGE KAWAMURA
description: Dissented, argued that the Constitution's plain language does not define what a "reading" entails or compel amendments to be germane, and the legislature's rules were properly followed.

name: McKenna, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part separately, arguing for different outcomes on specific sections of the petition.

name: Wilson, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part separately, joining Justice McKenna as to Sections I and III.A.

name: Eddins, J.
description: Concurred separately, likely providing additional or distinct reasoning for the decision.

name: NAKAYAMA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court erred in suppressing the evidence because it was not "fruit of the poisonous tree" as the State gained no benefit from the entry and Lee's independent actions (assaulting officers) severed the causal link.

name: WILSON J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority creates a new suicide exception to privacy rights, allowing warrantless entry into homes, and that the causal link between illegal entry and evidence was not severed.

name: RECKTENWALD, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority creates a new suicide exception to privacy rights, allowing warrantless entry into homes, and that the causal link between illegal entry and evidence was not severed.

name: MCKENNA, JJ.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority creates a new suicide exception to privacy rights, allowing warrantless entry into homes, and that the causal link between illegal entry and evidence was not severed.
